title: Valve timing check without pulling the timing cover: Dodge 318 (1976-77 truck)
summary: Checks for a stretched or jumped timing chain using a spacer and a dial indicator on the #1 intake valve.

steps.text: Turn the crankshaft until the number six exhaust valve is closing and the number six intake valve is opening.
Slip a 1/4 in spacer between the rocker arm pad and the valve stem tip of the number one intake valve (the second valve on the left bank).
Mount a dial indicator so its plunger touches the valve spring retainer as close to perpendicular as you can get.
Let the spring pressure bleed the lifter down so it acts like a solid lifter, then zero the indicator.
Turn the crankshaft clockwise until the valve has lifted 0.010 in. The crankshaft pulley should now read between 10 degrees before TDC and 2 degrees after TDC. Remove the spacer.
Don't keep turning the crank clockwise with the spacer in: the valve spring can bottom out and damage the lifter.
If the reading is outside that range, check the sprocket index marks, inspect the timing chain for wear, and confirm the TDC mark on the timing indicator is accurate.

sources.title: TM 9-2320-266-34: Direct and General Support Maintenance Manual, Truck, Cargo, 1-1/4 Ton, 4x4 (M880 series)
sources.publisher: Headquarters, Department of the Army, January 1976 (reprint with Changes 1-7)
